original.description: Continuation of an adjudicable tenancy issue is analytically separate from proving dispossession and from injunction discretion. The judgment describes Section 6 recovery for loss of settled possession without consent otherwise than by due course of law, but also recounts the rule that unlawful possession cannot be protected against the true owner by injunction; discretionary factors require separate assessment.
original.conclusion_text: Procedural survival of the tenancy issue cannot itself establish forcible dispossession, a right to Section 6 recovery, or entitlement to injunction; relevant evidence and discretionary injunction standards must be assessed separately in the appropriate trial proceedings.
original.jurisdiction: India; Supreme Court civil plaint-rejection review discussing Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and injunction principles
original.source_quote: The question of forcible possession as claimed is also a matter which can be pressed into service by the parties before the trial Court and if raised the Court shall deal with it considering its relevance to the suit and accept it or otherwise reject the plea in accordance with law. We do not think it necessary to express any opinion in that regard.

scope_limits: Section 6 restoration and discretionary injunction are different questions: possible recovery despite lack of title does not itself justify injunction against a true owner.

The judgment recounts a rule against injunction for a person in unlawful possession against the true owner, but does not find that these specific plaintiffs were unlawful possessors or that an injunction is due or barred on their merits.
The Supreme Court expressly leaves forcible-dispossession issues to the trial court if raised and relevant, and offers no view on the merits.
Claims about arrears, compliance with prior High Court orders, and surrender by other tenants are trust-side submissions or matters left for trial; their significance cannot be presumed.
The separate objection that only the District Court had jurisdiction was not specifically urged below and received no Supreme Court ruling.
